newsitem.title: POLAND: Poles believe country penetrated by foreign agents.
newsitem.headline: Poles believe country penetrated by foreign agents.

text.p: Some two thirds of Poles are convinced the country's political and economic life is influenced by foreign intelligence services, according to a survey published on Saturday.

The survey carried out by the independed PBS polling institute for the daily Rzeczpospolita showed 64 percent of Poles believed foreign secret services had an influence on the country's politics and 61 percent believed there was also interference in the economy.
Only about 15 percent of those polled believed Poland was free from such influence.

The survey was carried out on February 22-23, a week after security chief Zbigniew Siemiatkowski caused a political uproar by saying Russian intelligence was preparing plans to discredit Poland and block its entry to NATO and the European Union.
Nearly 50 percent of those surveyed believed Poland was being penetrated by Russian secret agents and 20 percent were convinced the country was influenced by U.S. intelligence agencies.
